challenge.title: Community Economy Evidence Challenge
challenge.description: Complete 10 activities: five clue-and-conclusion decisions and five matching tasks. Both parts of an evidence decision count together as one activity. Get at least 7 activities correct. All supplied lesson clues are available without saving them in your journal.

badge.name: Community Economy Investigator
badge.description: Earned by completing all five Chapter 9 missions and passing the evidence challenge. Recognizes supported explanations of tribute, labor, agricultural rules, trade and community effects.

evidence.question: A caption calls required tribute a gift freely offered by everyone. Which clue directly checks the meaning of tribute?
choices: Tribute was demanded under colonial authority, rather than simply offered as a gift
Every payment proves agreement
Tribute was always optional
A receipt reveals every private motive
evidence.explanation: Identify the required payment before explaining its effects. Payment does not establish freely chosen giving.

evidence.question: A delivery note is paired with a promise to pay later. Which clue directly checks whether the producer received payment?
choices: A payment promise is not proof that payment was received
Delivery proves every promise was fulfilled
Every producer freely chose the transaction
An order establishes every stage of the transaction
evidence.explanation: Separate delivery from payment. Find appropriate payment evidence for that transaction.

evidence.question: A rule requires a grower to use one buyer. Which clue directly explains the change in selling options?
choices: A required buyer can limit where a grower sells
Every sale allows identical buyer choice
A sale guarantees household wealth
Every crop everywhere followed this rule
evidence.explanation: Examine the options allowed by the rule without extending it beyond its documented scope.

evidence.question: An object was loaded in Manila. Which clue directly checks a claim that it must have been made there?
choices: A loading port is not necessarily the production place
Every cargo item was made at its loading port
Departure proves safe arrival
All objects had the same maker
evidence.explanation: Identify production evidence separately from the port where an item was loaded.

evidence.question: Two households face the same demand but start with different resources. Which clue directly checks the claim that their remaining resources must be equal?
choices: The same demand can leave households with different resources
Equal demands guarantee equal burdens
A model token is a documented historical peso
Every household had identical needs
evidence.explanation: Compare the resources and needs of each household. Equal amounts demanded do not establish identical effects.

matching.question: Match each tribute-investigation record with what it directly helps investigate.
matching.explanation: Demands, recorded collections and changed rules answer different questions. One record does not explain every household effect.

matching.question: Match the labor and produce terms with their meanings.
pairs: A commitment that still needs evidence of fulfillment
matching.explanation: Labor, produce delivery and payment stages should not be merged into one voluntary transaction.

matching.question: Match these agriculture-policy ideas with their careful descriptions.
pairs: A crop grown for sale, without guaranteed wealth
What remains after the relevant costs
Ending a particular rule or system
matching.explanation: Sales are not automatically profit. Ending one arrangement does not end all farming, exchange or taxation.

matching.question: Match each galleon-trade clue with the idea it supports.
pairs: A recorded journey stage, not guaranteed arrival
Contributors may be missing from an account
matching.explanation: The network depended on places and peoples work. Check each journeys evidence rather than generalize from one record.

matching.question: Match each community-effects question with what to investigate.
pairs: Resources and needs alongside the demand
Travel and work alongside other tasks
The problem raised, with its outcome checked separately
matching.explanation: Different households and records need their own evidence. Model tokens and calendar slots are not universal historical rates or quotas.
